spec_features.evidence: Defined at emostab/config.py:102 `MAX_RESPONSE_TOKENS = 4096`. Imported and used as the default `max_tokens` in run_rollouts (evaluation/protocol.py:13,39) which passes it to `model.generate_batch(..., max_tokens=max_tokens, ...)` (protocol.py:62). In the backends this becomes an enforced generation limit: vLLM `SamplingParams(... max_tokens=max_tokens ...)` (models/local.py:105-107) and HF `max_new_tokens=max_tokens` (models/local.py:167); openrouter passes max_tokens to the API (models/openrouter.py:43). So it actually bounds each assistant turn's generation length.
spec_features.notes: It is a generation length bound per turn, enforced via the sampling/API call. It is not a distress-based or conversation-level halt; it just caps tokens per response.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # cap on a single assistant turn (see DESIGN.md)

code_only_features.evidence: emostab/petri/run_petri.py:23 `MAX_AUDIT_TURNS = 20`; run_transcript loops `for _ in range(max_turns)` (run_petri.py:53) where max_turns defaults to MAX_AUDIT_TURNS (run_petri.py:47), bounding the auditor<->target conversation to 20 turns. The loop simply runs the fixed count; there is no distress-based early exit.
